summary: Console dashboard: top-n timeseries widget shows duplicated series after applying multiple tag filters
description:
Issue summary:
When customers apply multiple tag filters to a 'Top-N timeseries' widget (e.g., service.name and deployment.env), the widget occasionally renders duplicate series for the same logical entity (same service+deployment combination). Duplicates appear as separate lines with identical labels but different internal series IDs and slightly different point counts.

Impact:
- Inkling Health reports visual confusion and incorrect rollups in a customer-facing SLO dashboard.
- Affects decisioning workflows that rely on the top-n ranking (incorrect top-N selection).
- Reproducible on prod in eu-west and observed by at least two other enterprise customers via support chat.

Environment:
- Console (web) in prod: eu-west
- Dashboard widget: Top-N Timeseries (aggregation: sum over 1m, group by tag.key)
- Query backend: console-query-service v2.11.3 behind CDN
- Cache layer: in-memory per-tenant response cache (service-cache v3.0)

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Open customer SLO dashboard in eu-west tenant.
2) Add two tag filters: service.name = "ingest-worker" and deployment.env = "canary".
3) Set time window to last 6 hours and refresh.
4) Observe Top-N widget: duplicate lines appear for the same service, with identical labels but separate series counts.
5) Remove one filter and reapply it -> sometimes duplicates disappear; results vary between hard refresh vs. soft refresh.

Observed logs / traces / query ids:
- Example query id: qid=20260302-8b7a1 (console-query-service)
- Raw query returned two aggregation buckets with the same composite key after server-side normalization: "ingest-worker|canary" and "ingest-worker|canary#alias-2"
- Trace snippet (span ids): span=svc-query-23a, cache-hit=true, cache-key=tenant-345:topn:ingest-worker|canary
- Browser console: widget-mapper warns: "duplicate-series-detected" for widget_id=wdg-79

Additional notes:
- Customer reports that exporting the same widget to CSV yields a single logical row per entity (server-side CSV export did correct dedupe), suggesting the duplication is introduced at the widget rendering or client-side series mapping stage, but query payload does include both buckets in some cases.
- Occurs more frequently when tenant-level cache entries are near eviction and when small timing offsets happen between cache refresh and name-aliasing updates.

Expected behaviour:
- Top-N timeseries widget should deduplicate on the logical grouping key (service.name + deployment.env) after server-side normalization prior to rendering.

Workaround (customer-facing):
- Temporary: Toggle one of the tag filters off and on OR perform a hard browser refresh; in some cases this forces the widget to request a fresh query and returns a single series.
- For pipeline users: Use the CSV export for authoritative values until fix is deployed.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: client-side mapper bug — later adjusted after backend logs showed both buckets present in response.
Reproduction in staging required manipulating cache TTL and triggering name-alias normalization concurrently to hit the race window.
Root cause: non-idempotent alias rewrite in query-service normalization path leading to both aliased and unaliased aggregation buckets being included in responses when cache was partially updated.
Frontend should also defensively dedupe identical logical groupings to avoid visual anomalies in the event of future backend transient states.
Related regression: introduced in platform change 2.11.0 that modified aliasing behaviour — add to changelog and postmortem.
resolution: Fix deployed: made aliasing normalization idempotent at the query-service layer (v2.11.4) and added defensive dedupe in console-web widget mapper (v1.42.2). Verified with Inkling Health in eu-west; duplicates no longer appear. Follow-ups: add automated regression test that simulates concurrent alias and cache update, and add an alert to the console observability dashboard for 'duplicate-series-detected' events. Owner: Marco Liu (SRE) and Priya Shah (Frontend).
